Specification: This module specifies a two-procedure factorial algorithm translated from a PlusCal program. The algorithm uses mutually recursive procedures FactProc and FactProc2, together with an explicit call stack, to compute the factorial of 5 in the shared variable result, and then prints either a success or error message depending on whether the result is 120. The specification includes an initial predicate, action definitions for each control location, a next-state relation, a temporal specification with weak fairness on Next, a termination property asserting eventual arrival at pc = "Done", and a simple invariant that result always remains a natural number.
IfThenElse: IF arg1 = 0 THEN /\ pc' = Head(stack).pc /\ u' = Head(stack).u /\ arg1' = Head(stack).arg1 /\ stack' = Tail(stack) /\ UNCHANGED << result, arg2, u2 >> ELSE /\ result' = result * arg1 /\ /\ arg2' = arg1 - 1 /\ stack' = << [ procedure |->  "FactProc2", pc        |->  "b", u2        |->  u2, arg2      |->  arg2 ] >> \o stack /\ u2' = 1 /\ pc' = "p12" /\ UNCHANGED << arg1, u >>

IF arg2 = 0 THEN /\ pc' = Head(stack).pc /\ u2' = Head(stack).u2 /\ arg2' = Head(stack).arg2 /\ stack' = Tail(stack) /\ UNCHANGED << result, arg1, u >> ELSE /\ result' = result * arg2 /\ /\ arg1' = arg2 - 1 /\ stack' = << [ procedure |->  "FactProc", pc        |->  Head(stack).pc, u         |->  u, arg1      |->  arg1 ] >> \o Tail(stack) /\ u2' = Head(stack).u2 /\ u' = 1 /\ pc' = "p1" /\ arg2' = arg2
IF result = 120 THEN /\ PrintT(<<"Correct =", 120>>) ELSE /\ PrintT(<<"Error = ", result>>)
